title: Connect AI agents to Meta with MCP
snippet:
Meta runs official remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that bring Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Meta Ads capabilities to your agentic workflows.
**This page is documentation, not an MCP server.** Don’t add this page’s URL to your MCP client. Use one of these server URLs instead:
- Meta Ads MCP: `https://mcp.facebook.com/ads`
- Meta Social Technologies MCP: `https://mcp.facebook.com/devtools`
- WhatsApp Business Tools MCP: `https://mcp.facebook.com/whatsapp_business_tools`
## Benefits
- **One protocol, built for agent workflows.** Your agent connects to a Meta MCP server and discovers available tools at runtime. Tool descriptions, parameter schemas, and error responses are designed for large language models (LLMs) to interpret correctly. This design minimizes hallucination and failed tool calls.
- **Standard authentication.** OAuth-based authentication with permissions that you control from your Meta account settings. Each server defines its own permissions, so check the server-specific page for the ones it requests. Revoke access at any time.
## Available MCP servers
The following table lists the available Meta MCP servers:
| Server | Description | Type |
|---|---|---|
| [Meta Ads MCP](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/ads-ai-connectors/ads-mcp-server/ads-mcp-server-overview) | Manage Meta ads - analyze campaign performance, create and edit ads, campaigns, and catalogs, assess signal health, run experiments, review activity logs, and search help articles. Includes structured, permission-scoped access capabilities. | Remote MCP |
| [Meta Social Technologies MCP](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/mcp/devtools-mcp) | Manage the Meta apps and integrations you build on the Meta Social Technologies Developer Platform (developers.facebook.com) — configure webhooks, check compliance, review app status, monitor API health, and search developer documentation. Formerly known as Meta Developer Tools MCP. | Remote MCP |
| [WhatsApp Business Tools MCP](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/mcp/whatsapp-business-tools-mcp) | Manage your WhatsApp Business Platform integration — discover businesses and accounts, onboard and register phone numbers, manage message templates, configure webhooks, and send messages. | Remote MCP |
## Supported clients
The Meta team has validated these clients for general availability:
- Claude Desktop
- Claude Code
- ChatGPT
- Codex app
- Codex CLI
- Cursor app
- Cursor CLI

title: Get started
snippet:
To use the ads MCP server with your own Meta app, you must follow some key steps to set up your environment and gain access.
1. Go to [developers.facebook.com/apps](https://developers.facebook.com/apps) and create a new app, or open an existing app.
2. Add the **Create & manage ads with ads MCP server** use case.
## Authentication
The ads MCP server supports three authentication methods.
### OAuth
The MCP client redirects you to the Facebook Login for Business dialog. You sign in with your Facebook account or your Meta Managed Account (MMA) and approve the requested permissions. No manual token setup is required.
Make sure your Meta developer app’s **redirect URL** is configured correspondingly with your choice of MCP client in the [**Facebook Login for Business**](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/facebook-login/facebook-login-for-business) settings.
### User access token
### System user access token
You can also use a [system user access token](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-management-apis/system-users) to access the ads MCP server, for example for programmatic or server-to-server setups. See [System Users](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-management-apis/system-users) for how to create a system user and generate a token, requesting the permissions listed below.
> **Note:** Only **Employee**-role system user access tokens are supported. Admin-role system user access tokens can’t access the ads MCP server.
These permissions apply to both user access tokens and system user access tokens.
At a minimum, the token must be granted:
- `ads_mcp_management`
- `ads_read` or `ads_management`
Granting additional permissions enables access to more tools:
- `ads_management`
- `catalog_management`
- `business_management`
- `pages_show_list`
- `instagram_basic`
## Connect to ads MCP server
Sever URL of the ads MCP server
```
https://mcp.facebook.com/ads
```
### Connect to the ads MCP server from Claude Code
To add the ads MCP server to [Claude Code⁠](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fcode.claude.com%2Fdocs%2Fen%2Fmcp%23configure-mcp-servers&h=AUC5bBGUGImBlZXjHFuljLr-jPNMQdeMkB6W1l5Nm3KgA4IUjWDjNIpvSJGCRdWDwauRPFAUntEMH0JrvrYchk48YBo3t6p3gzGCwE1uWC4k8UiXghWGRsHAyZFqGa8_Ap0kzgEGkY6pPg), run the command below.
```
claude mcp add --transport http --client-id <META_APP_ID> meta-ads https://mcp.facebook.com/ads
```

title: Meta's ads MCP server is now available for developers
snippet:
Today, we are opening up our ads MCP server to any developer with their own Meta app. You can now connect your AI application directly to Meta's advertising capabilities, enabling your users to create and optimize campaigns, pull performance insights, manage product catalogs, and more through natural language. This means any developer can now bring Meta's ads MCP capabilities into the tools their customers already use — whether that's a marketing platform, a data warehouse, or a custom internal system.

## How do I connect using my own app?
1. Go to the [developer dashboard](https://developers.facebook.com/apps/) and select the app you'd like to use.
2. Click **Use cases** in the left navigation, then **Add use cases**.
3. In the popup, click **Ads and monetization**, select **Create & manage ads with ads MCP server**, and click **Save.**
4. **OPTIONAL** If you manage data on behalf of other businesses, for example you are an agency or a partner, you need to submit your app for review.
- Request Advanced Access on the *ads_mcp_management* permission.
- On the 'Use cases' screen, click **Customize** for the ads MCP server use case.
- On the 'Permissions and features' tab, click **Actions** to get Advanced Access, then click **Go to app review**.
5. Choose how to authenticate: [OAuth](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fmodelcontextprotocol.io%2Fdocs%2Ftutorials%2Fsecurity%2Fauthorization&h=AUBBNeQ2L1BivOSZqrQrKTIiYTDRTmioMAFYv0vAQJVLHohGRopCu3DpF9Pob1Qv17JP5kbx3_s_wjKCAxnyhZhgVYNb_0hPmOUPXYZksxAclNyaWJ6XQa1wC5IZBdk_EAkYjG7lO50jVMVC) for automatic token handling via Facebook Login for Business, or pass a pre-obtained access token if you manage your own token lifecycle.
## Managing agent controls programmatically
Connecting an agent to an ad account raises an obvious question: can you control what the agent does? Yes - via ads MCP server rules. Rules define the actions an AI agent can and cannot take on a given ad account or catalog. For example, you can grant an agent read access to performance data while withholding the ability to make changes to budgets, campaigns, or creative.
Until now, those rules could only be set one asset at a time in Meta Business Suite settings. That is workable for a single advertiser but impractical for users operating at scale.

title: Connect an MCP client to Meta
snippet:
Use this guide to connect a supported AI client to a remote Meta MCP server and authorize access with OAuth. When you finish, your client can discover and execute the server's available tools.
## Before you begin
To connect a client, you need:
- A current version of a supported AI client.
- A Meta account with access to the assets that the server manages. Assets are the businesses, apps, and accounts that you select when you grant consent.
- A Meta app, only if the server-specific page requires a client ID.
Open the documentation for the MCP server that you want to use, starting from the [list of available Meta MCP servers](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/mcp#available-mcp-servers). A client is supported on a given server only if that server's page lists it.

For example, connecting to the Meta Ads MCP server with your own Meta app uses this path. Its [Get started](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/ads-ai-connectors/ads-mcp-server/ads-mcp-server-get-started) page describes the app setup and redirect URL.
The Meta MCP servers listed on this site use OAuth public clients with Proof Key for Code Exchange. Don't enter or share an App Secret.
## Connect your client
To connect a Meta MCP server, choose `<SERVER_ALIAS>` as a short local identifier without spaces, such as `meta_server`. Replace `<SERVER_URL>` with the URL from the server-specific page. Replace `<META_APP_ID>` with your Meta app's App ID only when that page requires a client ID.
Graphical clients ask for a server name rather than a local alias. In those clients, use the server name from the server-specific page, which can contain spaces.
For example, the Meta Social Technologies MCP server publishes the URL `https://mcp.facebook.com/devtools`, so a complete Codex CLI command with the alias `meta_devtools` is:
```bash
codex mcp add meta_devtools --url https://mcp.facebook.com/devtools
```

To authenticate with the Meta MCP server again, use your client's authentication controls. In Codex CLI, clear the current authorization and start a new sign-in, using the `<SERVER_ALIAS>` that you chose in [Connect your client](#connect-your-client):
```bash
codex mcp logout <SERVER_ALIAS>
codex mcp login <SERVER_ALIAS>
```
In Claude Code, clear the stored credentials and start a new sign-in:
```bash
claude mcp logout <SERVER_ALIAS>
claude mcp login <SERVER_ALIAS>
```
You can also select **Clear authentication** or **Re-authenticate** on the server in the `/mcp` panel.

title: GitHub - bartlomiejborzucki/meta-ads-agent: Meta Ads agent toolkit for Codex and Claude Code: campaign planning, validation, previews and reporting via Meta's official Ads MCP server.
snippet:
**Turn a coding agent into a careful Meta Ads operator.**
Twelve skills, a validated campaign plan, resumable state, and an approval gate on anything that spends — built on Meta's **official** Ads MCP server, for Claude Code, Codex, and any agent that reads Markdown skills.

You:    Build a campaign for this webinar. 70 PLN/day, Poland, three angles.
Agent:  [writes a plan, validates it, shows it to you]
[creates campaign, ad set, creative, 3 ads — all PAUSED]
[renders previews for Feed, Instagram Feed, Stories, Reels]
"Created, all PAUSED. One issue: the Stories crop cuts the headline.
Nothing is spending. Fix the crop, or activate as is?"

**Meta's MCP does the work.** Meta ships a first-party MCP server at `https://mcp.facebook.com/ads` with about **100 tools** (104 on 2026-11-04) — accounts, campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, previews, insights, audiences, datasets, pixel rules, catalogs, experiments, activity logs and Ad Library search. It authenticates through your browser with Meta OAuth and is generally available. So this project does **not** rebuild the Marketing API: six of the eleven community projects in [the ecosystem audit](/bartlomiejborzucki/meta-ads-agent/blob/master/docs/research/ecosystem-audit.md) do, and it is a maintenance treadmill with a shrinking payoff.

**The fallback is being retired.** An optional layer built on Meta's official [`facebook-business`](https://github.com/meta/facebook-python-business-sdk) SDK covered seven things the MCP could not do: local image and video upload, video, existing-post, multi-variant / placement-specific and carousel creatives, and deletion. As of **2026-11-04 the MCP does all seven** - `ads_creative_upload_media`, `ads_create_creative` with `video_id`, `cards`, `multi_media`, `placement_customizations`, `object_story_id` and `source_instagram_media_id`, a PAUSED `ads_boost_ig_post`, and `ads_update_entity` with `status: DELETED` ([ADR-012](/bartlomiejborzucki/meta-ads-agent/blob/master/docs/architecture/adr/ADR-012-mcp-coverage-and-draft-mode.md)).
